sutta:
Monks, the great sāla trees, supported by the Himalaya, the king of mountains, grow in five growths.

What five? They grow in branches, leaves, and foliage; they grow in bark, shoots, and pith; they grow in heartwood. Monks, the great sāla trees, supported by the Himalaya, the king of mountains, grow in these five growths.

Even so, monks, folk within a home, supported by a believing clan chief, grow in five growths. What five? They grow in faith, in virtue, in learning, in generosity, and they grow in wisdom. Monks, folk within the home, supported by a believing clan chief, grow in these five growths.
commentary: These five things that a lay person can grow in are very important good qualities: faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom. Faith refers to faith in the Triple Gem: the Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha. Growing in this faith is one of the very good things. Virtue means being virtuous, having good moral conduct, and keeping the precepts. Learning means knowledge of the Dhamma, the Buddha's teachings (the suttas). Growing in generosity means becoming less selfish, more generous, and more open-handed; as the Buddha says, whatever people ask of you, you try to give if you can. And the fifth is wisdom. To grow in wisdom is a natural result of learning and meditation. Supported by a believing clan chief, a person can grow in these ways.

quiz.quote: According to the teacher, how does one grow in wisdom?

options.title: Meditation Only
options.body: Wisdom is purely a result of sitting in silence without any study.

options.title: Natural Result
options.body: To grow in wisdom is a natural result of learning and meditation.

options.title: Social Status
options.body: Wisdom is granted to those who achieve a high rank in the clan.

options.title: Random Luck
options.body: Wisdom grows spontaneously and cannot be cultivated through effort.

quiz.teacherSummary: The teacher states clearly that wisdom is not accidental—it is the direct outcome of combining Dhamma study (learning) with meditative practice.

japaneseAudio.text: 説法者は、知恵は偶然に得られるものではなく、仏法の学習（聞）と瞑想の実践を組み合わせることによる直接的な成果であると明確に述べています。
